headline: Fed holds, eyes December hike; Jio debut lifts Reliance past Tata

segments.title: The big picture
segments.script:
Good morning, and welcome to your Market Brief for Thursday, the twenty-ninth of October.

Three things matter most today. First, the US Federal Reserve held interest rates overnight, but two officials wanted a hike, and bond traders now see about a ninety percent chance of one in December. Second, Jio Platforms had a blockbuster debut, closing nearly twenty-seven percent above its issue price, and the Reliance group has overtaken the Tata group as India's most valuable business house. And third, oil stays the big worry, with Brent crude hovering around 114 dollars a barrel.

stories.title: US Fed holds interest rates at 3.75%-4% in 10-2 vote; two officials seek hike as inflation stays elevated
Jio listing propels Reliance past Tata Group as India's biggest conglomerate

segments.title: How markets closed
segments.script:
Wednesday was a rough ride. At one point the Sensex was down nearly 1,000 points, and the Nifty touched 22,500. VK Vijayakumar of Geojit said the market turned weak on reports of possible renewed US strikes on Iran after the American midterm elections. A late recovery trimmed the damage. The Sensex closed down 353 points at 73,246, and the Nifty slipped 51 points to 22,699.

Information technology did the most harm. The Nifty IT index fell about four percent, with Infosys, TCS and Coforge down as much as five percent. That came after IT had rallied twelve percent this month. Oil and gas stocks also fell more than two percent, led by Reliance Industries. On the other side, autos and some banks found buyers.

Several big names hit 52-week lows, including HDFC Bank, ITC, HDFC Life, Nestle and Britannia. Meanwhile PVR Inox, Indian Hotels, Piramal Pharma and Sona Comstar touched fresh highs.

Now to the flows. Foreign institutional investors extended their buying streak, putting in 871 crore rupees. Domestic institutions also bought, about 643 crore rupees. The rupee weakened against the dollar on higher oil.

The levels to watch: analysts quoted by Moneycontrol see 22,800 as the key resistance for the Nifty, with 22,500 to 22,400 as support, and then 22,200. Early signals this morning are mixed, with GIFT Nifty swinging either side of flat.

segments.title: IPOs and deals
segments.script:
Jio Platforms closed its first day at 1,417 rupees and 35 paise, about 26.7 percent above the issue price of 1,119 rupees. It is now India's second most valuable company, worth more than 13 lakh crore rupees, ahead of Bharti Airtel. The Economic Times says that puts it among the five biggest telecom companies in the world. Dealmakers told Moneycontrol that Jio has paved the way for more large companies to list in India.

In the primary market today, Bombay Coated and Special Steels opens its issue. It raised 54 crore rupees from anchor investors, and the issue closes on the second of November.

On the deals side, Cholamandalam Investment's board approved raising up to 5,000 crore rupees through a qualified institutional placement. And MSCI has put the removal of Polycab India from its indices on hold, because an appeals tribunal stayed the company's admission into insolvency.

segments.title: Results roundup
segments.script:
Let's start with autos. Hero MotoCorp's profit rose 41 percent to about 1,861 crore rupees, on revenue up 23 percent to nearly 14,971 crore rupees. Scooter sales jumped 47 percent, and retail sales of its electric Vida scooters rose 76 percent.

Now to consumer goods. Hindustan Unilever's turnover rose 15 percent to 18,071 crore rupees, a fourteen-quarter high, with volumes up 7 percent and home care sales up 22 percent. But profit rose only 4 percent, the company flagged inflation and rural wage pressure, and the stock is near a six-year low. United Breweries was the star, with profit up 190 percent and margins up nearly five percentage points, sending the stock up 15 percent. It has warned, though, that profit growth will slow this quarter as costs rise.

In metals, Vedanta's profit jumped 151 percent on revenue up 57 percent to 25,812 crore rupees, and it cut debt by 4,624 crore rupees in the quarter. Vedanta Aluminium's profit roughly doubled to 6,187 crore rupees. Adani Enterprises went the other way. Revenue rose 75 percent to 37,216 crore rupees, but profit fell 55 percent against a one-time gain a year ago.

In lending, Cholamandalam's profit rose 41 percent to 1,630 crore rupees. Satin Creditcare's profit more than tripled to 176 crore rupees, with bad loans down to 1.9 percent from 3.5 percent. And Piramal Pharma surged up to 18 percent after a surprise profit. Today, watch for Asian Paints and Trent.

segments.title: Economy and policy
segments.script:
Factory output is cooling. The index of industrial production grew 6.7 percent in September, down from 8 percent in August and a four-month low, as mining contracted. Manufacturing still grew 7.6 percent, and economists quoted by the Economic Times expect growth for the September quarter above 7 percent. RBI Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta said growth would have topped 8 percent but for global shocks, and that India is the only large emerging economy set to cut its government debt ratio by 2031.

The Cabinet had a busy day. It approved a 3 percent dearness allowance hike for central employees and pensioners, effective from the first of July, costing about 10,016 crore rupees. It cleared a 10,000 crore rupee scheme to raise container-making capacity tenfold, and 7,395 crore rupees to strengthen gram panchayats. Separately, the textiles incentive scheme has been extended to 2033-34, with the minimum turnover for some makers halved to 100 crore rupees.

On trade, India and Mexico have formally begun talks on a preferential trade agreement.

And on oil, the rating agency Icra estimates fuel retailers could lose over 64,000 crore rupees on petrol and diesel this financial year if crude stays between 105 and 115 dollars and pump prices are not raised. Former RBI governor Raghuram Rajan said a weaker rupee is not necessarily bad, and warned against draining reserves to defend it.

segments.title: Around the world
segments.script:
The Federal Reserve held rates at 3.75 to 4 percent in a ten to two vote, with two officials pushing for a hike. Chair Kevin Warsh said fighting inflation is the priority, and announced fewer rate-setting meetings from next year. The ten-year US yield is around 5 percent. Wall Street still ended mostly higher.

Big Tech results are steering sentiment. Alphabet's revenue grew 25 percent to about 127.6 billion dollars, but missed estimates, and profit fell on an 8.7 billion dollar investment loss. Its shares slid about 9 percent after hours. Microsoft, on the other hand, beat estimates on strong cloud growth.

On oil, Brent is around 114 dollars, just off four-year highs. Moneycontrol reports that mediator talks on West Asia continue, and that Iran is working on a seven-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Gold slipped after the Fed decision.

segments.title: Stories you're following
segments.script: An update on the Jio IPO you're following. The shares ended listing day nearly 27 percent above the issue price, lifting the Reliance group past the Tata group. Motilal Oswal, Elara Capital and Dolat Capital have joined Nomura in starting coverage, with targets that the Economic Times says point to as much as 28 percent upside.

segments.title: Your money
segments.script:
A few changes for your wallet. From the first of November, Sebi chief Tuhin Kanta Pandey says direct plans will be the default on fund houses' own digital platforms, and anyone choosing a regular plan must be told about its higher expense ratio. Sebi will also issue a paper on easing compliance for foreign investors.

On GST, two things. From the first of November, small online sellers can register in another state using an e-commerce warehouse as their local base, subject to conditions. And the government has clarified that brokerage paid by overseas clients may count as an export of services, which could spare foreign investors the 18 percent GST on it.

For central government staff and pensioners, the 3 percent dearness allowance hike applies retrospectively from the first of July. Farmers can expect the twenty-fourth PM-Kisan instalment, over 18,680 crore rupees, on the thirtieth. And the Centre has cut the maximum retail prices of some trade-margin-capped cancer medicines by up to 93 percent.

One investor note. More Indians are investing abroad, and the Economic Times reports that the RBI's limits on overseas investment are nearing their cap, pushing some investors towards GIFT City.

That's the brief. Today, watch whether the Nifty can get past 22,800, how Jio trades on its second day, results from Asian Paints and Trent, and oil near 114 dollars. Have a good day.
